terra.problem: “If it exists, it's on the list” includes God and the Son among created things, which the passage does not say.
The joke uses the Son holding all things together as a comic contrast with Papa dropping cookie boxes. His humor must not target Jesus or His work.
The half-cookie-box joke makes God's fullness the subject of the comparison, rather than keeping the humor on the human side.
Exodus 19:20 says God called Moses up Mount Sinai; it does not say Moses received the law there. The reference does not support the stated fact.
The statement that offerings appear in the Bible is a Bible fact from outside this passage and has no reference.
The explanation identifies Christ as the one who reconciled them, but the passage says God reconciled them by Christ's physical body through death.
The statement that Moses brings the law is a Bible fact from outside this passage and has no reference.
The explanation states what Paul knows without marking it as Papa's inference. It also describes the whole letter as being about the Son having first place, which goes beyond the supplied passage.
